sentences.zh: 他不再适合演主角的好朋友了。

sentences.en: So is this when he goes to Vegas?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他去拉斯维加斯的时候吗？

sentences.en: He does go to Vegas, and he hates it.
sentences.zh: 他确实去了拉斯维加斯，而且他讨厌那里。

sentences.en: He absolutely hates it, going to Vegas and sort of doing a turn.
sentences.zh: 他非常讨厌去拉斯维加斯表演节目。

sentences.en: Because it's seen as a mark of failure, because he's kind of hosting cabaret shows.
sentences.zh: 因为这被视为失败的标志，毕竟他当时是在主持歌舞表演。

sentences.en: Exactly, hosting cabaret.
sentences.zh: 没错，主持歌舞表演。

sentences.en: He does a two-week stint, I think it is, and he really doesn't like it at all.
sentences.zh: 我想他大概在那里待了两周，他真的很不喜欢。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He thinks it's tawdry.
sentences.zh: 他觉得那很俗气。

sentences.en: He thinks it's humiliating.
sentences.zh: 他觉得那很丢人。

sentences.en: And it's at this point, or pretty much at this point, that he is approached.
sentences.zh: 就在这个时候，或者说差不多在这个时候，有人找上了他。

sentences.en: In his capacity at the Screen Actors Guild, he had done a deal to allow his own agency, MCA, to move into TV production.
sentences.zh: 他以美国演员工会负责人的身份，达成了一项协议，允许他自己的经纪公司MCA进军电视制作领域。

sentences.en: Previously, agencies were not allowed to get involved with TV production.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，经纪公司是不允许参与电视制作的。

sentences.en: He broke us a deal.
sentences.zh: 他为我们谈成了一笔交易。

sentences.en: And about a year or so later, two years later, MCA come to him.
sentences.zh: 大约一年或两年后，MCA找到了他。

sentences.en: This guy called Taft Schreiber comes to him and says,
sentences.zh: 一个叫塔夫特·施赖伯的人找到他说：

sentences.en: We've had an offer for you, and I think this is perfect.
sentences.zh: 我们为你争取到了一个机会，我觉得这非常完美。

sentences.en: So General Electric are sponsoring a program called General Electric Theatre.
sentences.zh: 通用电气正在赞助一个叫《通用电气剧场》的节目。

sentences.en: It's been running off and on, but they really want to invest in it.
sentences.zh: 这个节目断断续续播了一阵子，但他们真的很想加大投入。

sentences.en: They want to make it a weekly thing, and they need a hoSt.
sentences.zh: 他们想把它做成周播节目，而且需要一个主持人。

sentences.en: So basically, MCA clients will appear on TV.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，MCA的客户都会出现在电视上。

sentences.en: It's an anthology.
sentences.zh: 这是一个选集剧。

sentences.en: They'll appear in a series of plays.
sentences.zh: 他们会出现在一系列戏剧中。

sentences.en: And we think it will be a ratings top, it'll be a massive hit, and General Electric are going to put in a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这会收视率登顶，成为巨大的热门，通用电气也会投入大量资金。

sentences.en: We need a host to do a two-minute introduction to give it a sense of coherence.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个主持人来做两分钟的开场白，让节目更有连贯性。

sentences.en: But also, the host must be a goodwill ambassador for General Electric.
sentences.zh: 但同时，主持人必须是通用电气的亲善大使。

sentences.en: So there will be a lot of work touring General Electric plants, giving speeches, meeting the workers, being the kind of face of General Electric.
sentences.zh: 所以会有很多工作，比如巡回参观通用电气的工厂、发表演讲、会见工人，成为通用电气的门面。

sentences.en: You see, when I read about this, I had not understood that 30 Rock, the Tina Fey sitcom about a comedy show.
sentences.zh: 你看，当我读到这些时，我还没明白《我为喜剧狂》这部蒂娜·菲关于喜剧节目的情景喜剧。

sentences.en: And it's all owned by General Electric.
sentences.zh: 它完全是由通用电气拥有的。

sentences.en: And I never understood why, what General Electric were doing involved in a kind of comedy show.
sentences.zh: 我一直不明白为什么，通用电气为什么要参与这种喜剧节目。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But now I understand.
sentences.zh: 但现在我明白了。

sentences.en: It's obviously a kind of long-running tradition in America.
sentences.zh: 这显然是美国一种由来已久的传统。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the firm would sponsor the show.
sentences.zh: 所以公司会赞助节目。

sentences.en: If the firm walked away, the show ends.
sentences.zh: 如果公司撤资，节目就结束了。

sentences.en: That's where the money for the show is coming from.
sentences.zh: 节目的资金来源就是这样。

sentences.en: So General Electric are offering to pay Reagan $125,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 所以通用电气提出每年支付里根12.5万美元。

sentences.en: That's the equivalent of $3 million a year today, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我想这相当于今天的300万美元。

sentences.en: And General Electric have a really, really sort of ruthless and cunning attitude towards advertising and getting their message across.
sentences.zh: 通用电气在广告宣传和传达理念方面有着非常冷酷且狡猾的态度。

sentences.en: So you're talking about people having excellent names.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到的这些人名字都很响亮。

sentences.en: The man running their ad account is called Earl Dunkel.
sentences.zh: 负责他们广告业务的人叫厄尔·邓克尔。

sentences.en: But the real guiding spirit of man who's in charge of their labor relations is Lemuel Boulware.
sentences.zh: 但真正负责劳资关系的精神领袖是勒缪尔·鲍尔沃。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Boulwareism, as it's called, involves basically you use your own workers as the advert for your company.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“鲍尔沃主义”，基本上就是利用你自己的员工来为公司做广告。

sentences.en: You persuade your own workers of the virtue of your company.
sentences.zh: 你要让自己的员工相信公司的美德。

sentences.en: So in other words, Boulwareism was you persuade your workers that government intervention and regulation have gone too far, that free enterprise is the American way, free market,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，鲍尔沃主义就是让你说服员工，政府的干预和监管已经过头了，自由企业才是美国之道，自由市场，

sentences.en: all this stuff, anti-communism and low taxes.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西，反共产主义和低税收。

sentences.en: And so by this time, Reagan is buying into this.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，里根已经开始接受这一套了。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: 1952 is the first time he votes Republican, right?
sentences.zh: 1952年是他第一次投票给共和党，对吧？

sentences.en: Eisenhower.
sentences.zh: 艾森豪威尔。

sentences.en: And he felt a little bit bad about it because his father had always been such a keen Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他当时感到有点内疚，因为他的父亲一直是个坚定的民主党人。

sentences.en: And he actually says at the time there are things about Adlai Stevenson, the Democratic candidate, that I quite like.
sentences.zh: 他当时甚至说，民主党候选人阿德莱·史蒂文森身上有些东西我还是挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: However, it sort of makes sense that Reagan is moving rightwards.
sentences.zh: 然而，里根向右转也是情理之中的事。

sentences.en: He is rich.
sentences.zh: 他很有钱。

sentences.en: All his friends in Hollywood, the people that he hangs out with, as we were saying before, they're quite right-wing.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前所说，他在好莱坞的所有朋友，他交往的人，都相当右倾。

sentences.en: Nancy is quite right-wing.
sentences.zh: 南希也相当右倾。

sentences.en: But also he's reading, as you said, the Reader's DigeSt.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，他也在读《读者文摘》。

sentences.en: He's also become absolutely addicted to a periodical called Human Events, which is, again, very, very firmly right-wing.
sentences.zh: 他还对一本叫《人类事件》的期刊上瘾了，那也是非常非常坚定的右翼刊物。

sentences.en: So he's being radicalized by mid-market magazines.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在被这些大众市场杂志激进化。

sentences.en: Yes, he actually is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And when he goes to General Electric, that radicalizes him further.
sentences.zh: 当他去了通用电气，这进一步激化了他。

sentences.en: And he, by the way, the interesting thing is not the two-minute introductions to the episodes, it's the tours, because he turns out to be absolutely brilliant at it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，有趣的地方不在于那两分钟的开场白，而在于巡回演讲，因为他在这方面表现得极其出色。

sentences.en: He will go to the plant.
sentences.zh: 他会去工厂。

sentences.en: There is a wonderful description of this in-
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有很棒的描述——

sentences.en: Bob Spitz.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·斯皮茨。

sentences.en: Bob Spitz.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·斯皮茨。

sentences.en: Bob Spitz.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·斯皮茨。

sentences.en: But also other writers, as Gary Wills wrote about this in his book, Reagan's America, Innocence at Home, in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 还有其他作家，比如加里·威尔斯在80年代的书《里根的美国：家中的纯真》中也写过。

sentences.en: The General Electric was the key to Reagan.
sentences.zh: 通用电气是了解里根的关键。

sentences.en: As Bob Spitz describes it, Reagan goes into the plant.
sentences.zh: 正如鲍勃·斯皮茨所描述的那样，里根走进工厂。

sentences.en: And at first, people are sort of staring at him.
sentences.zh: 起初，人们只是盯着他看。

sentences.en: And his technique is he will usually talk to the women, because they're delighted to see a Hollywood matinee idol, you know, a film star.
sentences.zh: 他的技巧是通常先和女性交谈，因为她们很高兴见到好莱坞的当红偶像，你知道的，电影明星。

sentences.en: And the men are a little bit suspicious.
sentences.zh: 而男人们则有点怀疑。

sentences.en: And then after he's talked to the women and they've all sort of gushed over him, he then goes over to the men and he makes a few jokes.
sentences.zh: 等他跟女性聊完，她们都对他赞不绝口后，他再走向男人们，讲几个笑话。

sentences.en: He tells them a few jokes about the women often.
sentences.zh: 他经常给他们讲一些关于女性的笑话。

sentences.en: And he puts the men at their ease.
sentences.zh: 他让男人们放松下来。

sentences.en: And very, very quickly, they get into kind of banter and gossip.
sentences.zh: 很快，他们就开始互相打趣和闲聊了。

sentences.en: And he tells Hollywood stories.
sentences.zh: 他讲起好莱坞的故事。

sentences.en: He's one of the boys.
sentences.zh: 他成了他们中的一员。

sentences.en: He has this film-style glamour, of course.
sentences.zh: 他当然有一种电影明星般的魅力。

sentences.en: He's tanned and he's tall and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他皮肤黝黑，身材高大等等。

sentences.en: But he has such an affable, down-to-earth manner.
sentences.zh: 但他有一种非常和蔼可亲、脚踏实地的态度。

sentences.en: He's brilliant at putting people at their ease.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长让人感到放松。

sentences.en: He's one of the guys.
sentences.zh: 他是他们中的一员。

sentences.en: He's absolutely one of the boys.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是他们中的一员。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And then as part of this, he gives after-dinner speeches.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，他还会发表餐后演讲。

sentences.en: So General Electric starts to organise.
sentences.zh: 所以通用电气开始组织这些活动。

sentences.en: He'll talk to the Rotary Club or the Chamber of Commerce or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他会去扶轮社或商会之类的机构演讲。

sentences.en: And the speeches that he gives are, he'll start with some jokes and some Hollywood anecdotes and be self-deprecating.
sentences.zh: 他发表的演讲通常以笑话和好莱坞轶事开头，并进行自我调侃。

sentences.en: And then he'll start talking a little bit about politics, not in an excessively partisan way.
sentences.zh: 然后他会开始谈论一点政治，但不会过于党派化。

sentences.en: So in other words, if you're a Democrat, you can still enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，即使你是民主党人，你也能听得津津有味。

sentences.en: But he'll say things that lots of people kind of agree with in a slightly kind of golf clubby, you know, man at the bar kind of way.
sentences.zh: 但他会说一些很多人都同意的话，就像在高尔夫俱乐部或酒吧里聊天那样。

sentences.en: He'll say, we pay a lot of taxes and what do we get for them?
sentences.zh: 他会说，我们交了那么多税，到底得到了什么？

sentences.en: You know, those people in Washington, they're all the same.
sentences.zh: 你知道，华盛顿的那些人，他们都一个样。

sentences.en: Don't you just love our country and you hate people running it down?
sentences.zh: 难道你不爱我们的国家吗？你难道不讨厌那些诋毁它的人吗？

sentences.en: Communism, we've got to stand up to that.
sentences.zh: 共产主义，我们必须站出来对抗它。

sentences.en: You know, he'll come out with all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他会说出所有这些话。

sentences.en: Most people will just nod and say, this is great.
sentences.zh: 大多数人只会点头说，说得太好了。

sentences.en: And what Reagan does that is brilliant, and he gets this from Reader's Digest and whatnot, is he wraps it up in parables and little stories.
sentences.zh: 里根最厉害的地方在于——他从《读者文摘》之类的地方学到的——他把这些观点包装在寓言和小故事里。

sentences.en: His increasingly right-wing convictions, are they any more sophisticated than, oh, it's terrible, they're taking all our tax.
sentences.zh: 他那日益右倾的信念，难道比“哦，太糟糕了，他们拿走了我们所有的税”更深刻吗？

sentences.en: You know, they're taking too much tax.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们收了太多的税。

sentences.en: Commies, they're awful.
sentences.zh: 共产党人，他们太可怕了。

sentences.en: Does he have a kind of a more sophisticated understanding of geopolitics, of how the economy works or anything?
sentences.zh: 他是否对地缘政治、经济运作方式有更深刻的理解？

sentences.en: Or is it just kind of gut, this is what I think?
sentences.zh: 还是说这仅仅是一种直觉，这就是我的想法？

sentences.en: Well, it's not just completely empty because he's reading these periodicals.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这并不完全是空洞的，因为他在阅读这些期刊。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he's got loads of...
sentences.zh: 所以他有很多……

sentences.en: But it's not, I mean, it's not the Wall Street Journal, is it?
sentences.zh: 但那并不是《华尔街日报》，对吧？

sentences.en: No, and he's not reading Edmund Burke.
sentences.zh: 不，他也没在读埃德蒙·伯克。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not pondering whether Viscount Bolingbrook was the real father of, you know, intellectual conservatism.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他并没有在思考博林布鲁克子爵是否是知识保守主义的真正鼻祖。

sentences.en: No, but he's not reading, I don't know, strategic analysis from top geopoliticians or anything.
sentences.zh: 不，他也没在读什么顶级地缘政治学家的战略分析之类的东西。

sentences.en: He's not Margaret Thatcher reading Hayek or Dostoevsky.
sentences.zh: 他不是读哈耶克或陀思妥耶夫斯基的玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: He's absolutely not that at all.
sentences.zh: 他绝对不是那样的人。

sentences.en: And nor is he ever reading anything that would possibly contradict him.
sentences.zh: 而且他从来不读任何可能反驳他的东西。

sentences.en: So he's reading things that confirm his, I was going to say prejudices, that's the wrong word.
sentences.zh: 所以他读的东西都是在证实他的——我本来想说偏见，但这个词不对。

sentences.en: They confirm all his instincts.
sentences.zh: 它们证实了他所有的直觉。

sentences.en: And that is kind of the key, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这才是关键，不是吗？

sentences.en: That is the key.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键。

sentences.en: But he doesn't need to kind of, I mean, so often politicians whose opinions are kind of informed by detailed study or academic study or whatever,
sentences.zh: 但他不需要那种……我是说，很多政客的观点是基于详细的研究或学术研究之类的，

sentences.en: they have to kind of lower it down a grade when they're kind of making their pitch.
sentences.zh: 他们在发表观点时不得不降低一个档次。

sentences.en: And so it sounds condescending or bogus or false or hypocritical.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来很傲慢、虚假、伪善。

sentences.en: Whereas Reagan never had to do that because he is simply articulating what he feels.
sentences.zh: 而里根从来不需要那样做，因为他只是在表达自己的真实感受。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And his, you know, his radio frequency is the radio frequency of so many of his listeners.
sentences.zh: 而且他的无线电频率，就是他许多听众的无线电频率。

sentences.en: Brilliant way of putting it, Tom, actually.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这种说法真是太棒了。

sentences.en: I think it's exactly the right way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是最恰当的说法。

sentences.en: I think there's nothing contrived about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这没有任何矫揉造作的成分。

sentences.en: He reads up all the stuff.
sentences.zh: 他读了所有的东西。

sentences.en: He has all the facts.
sentences.zh: 他掌握了所有事实。

sentences.en: He has all the stories to back up what he believes.
sentences.zh: 他有各种故事来支撑他的信仰。

sentences.en: It's, as you say, it's what a lot of other people believe in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这正是 20 世纪 50 年代许多人所相信的。

sentences.en: So the funny thing is this is Eisenhower's America.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，这就是艾森豪威尔时代的美国。

sentences.en: So it's definitely not a kind of socialist state by any means.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，这绝对算不上是一种社会主义国家。

sentences.en: But there is a sense left over, I think, from antipathy to the New Deal that, you know, the government is regulating a lot, that we're paying too much tax, don't like communism,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，由于对“新政”的反感，人们心中仍有一种感觉，你知道，政府监管太多了，我们交的税太多了，不喜欢共产主义，

sentences.en: don't like interference, all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 不喜欢干预，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And Reagan is brilliant at articulating them.
sentences.zh: 而里根在表达这些观点方面非常出色。

sentences.en: As you say, it's not, you know, he's not kind of Ed Miliband.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他并不是，你知道，他不是埃德·米利班德那种人。

sentences.en: He hasn't been poring over policy documents.
sentences.zh: 他并没有钻研过政策文件。

sentences.en: Or indeed Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 或者说玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: No, it's not Margaret Thatcher either.
sentences.zh: 不，他也不是玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: What it is, he has an extraordinary gift to bring these things alive through human stories and to create a sense of empathy with his audience.
sentences.zh: 他的过人之处在于，他有一种非凡的天赋，能通过人类的故事让这些东西变得生动，并与听众产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And his affable, charming manner means that even people who don't necessarily agree with him still like him and enjoy the performance, actually.
sentences.zh: 他那和蔼可亲、充满魅力的举止意味着，即使是那些不一定同意他观点的人，实际上也喜欢他，并享受他的表演。

sentences.en: I mean, not everybody, of course.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当然不是所有人。

sentences.en: But all the time, he's becoming more right-wing.
sentences.zh: 但他一直在变得越来越右倾。

sentences.en: So I think it's not static.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这并非一成不变。

sentences.en: So he's been radicalized.
sentences.zh: 所以他被激进化了。

sentences.en: He's talking to plant managers who say to him, well, the government red tape stops us.
sentences.zh: 他与工厂经理交谈，他们对他说，政府的繁文缛节阻碍了我们。
